python.title: The walrus operator :=
python.text: Since Python 3.8 you can assign a value right inside an expression — handy in while and if.
python.code:
while (line := input()) != "exit":
    print(line)

python.title: f-strings with =
python.text: An = inside an f-string prints both the expression and its value. Perfect for debugging (Python 3.8+).

python.title: else on loops
python.text: for and while loops can have an else block — it runs only if the loop finished without a break.

python.title: Chained comparisons
python.text: Comparisons can be chained, just like in math.
python.code:
x = 5
print(1 < x < 10)       # True
print(1 < x > 3)        # True

python.title: Star unpacking
python.text: A star collects "everything else" into a list.
python.code:
first, *middle, last = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
print(middle)  # [2, 3, 4]

python.title: match / case
python.text: Python 3.10 added structural pattern matching — it can take data apart, not just compare values.
python.code:
match command.split():
    case ["go", direction]:
        print("going", direction)
    case ["quit"]:
        print("bye!")
    case _:
        print("unknown command")

python.title: Unlimited integers
python.text: Python's int never overflows: a number keeps growing as long as there is memory.

python.title: Caching in one line
python.text: The @cache decorator (Python 3.9+) remembers function results — recursion becomes instant.

python.title: Counter
python.text: collections.Counter counts elements in a single line.
python.code:
from collections import Counter
c = Counter("abracadabra")
print(c.most_common(2))  # [('a', 5), ('b', 2)]

python.title: enumerate with start
python.text: enumerate can start counting from any number, not just zero.
python.code:
for i, name in enumerate(["Python", "Java"], start=1):
    print(i, name)

python.title: zip(strict=True)
python.text: Plain zip silently cuts off the longer list. With strict=True (3.10+) it raises an error if the lengths differ.
python.code:
list(zip([1, 2, 3], "ab", strict=True))
# ValueError: zip() argument 2 is shorter than argument 1

python.title: Dicts keep order
python.text: Since Python 3.7 the insertion order of dict keys is guaranteed by the language.

python.title: Merging dicts with |
python.text: Since Python 3.9 dicts can be merged with the | operator, and |= updates in place.

python.title: pathlib and /
python.text: In pathlib, paths are joined with the / operator — no manual slashes or os.path.join.
python.code:
from pathlib import Path
p = Path("mods") / "finsfish" / "config.json"
print(p.suffix)  # .json

python.title: @dataclass
python.text: A dataclass writes __init__, __repr__ and __eq__ for you.

python.title: any and all
python.text: any() and all() work with generators and stop as soon as the answer is known.
python.code:
nums = [2, 4, 7, 8]
print(any(n % 2 for n in nums))  # True
print(all(n > 0 for n in nums))  # True

python.title: Trap: mutable default argument
python.text: A default value is created once, when the function is defined, not on every call.
python.code:
def add(item, bag=[]):
    bag.append(item)
    return bag

add(1); print(add(2))  # [1, 2] — surprise!
# fix: bag=None, then bag = bag or []

python.title: Underscores in numbers
python.text: Long numbers can be split with underscores — the value doesn't change.

python.title: itertools.pairwise
python.text: pairwise (3.10+) yields neighbouring pairs — handy for differences between elements.
python.code:
from itertools import pairwise
print(list(pairwise([1, 4, 9, 16])))
# [(1, 4), (4, 9), (9, 16)]

python.title: removeprefix / removesuffix
python.text: Since Python 3.9 strings can drop a prefix or suffix (unlike strip, which removes characters).
python.code:
print("minecraft:stone".removeprefix("minecraft:"))  # stone
print("photo.png".removesuffix(".png"))            # photo

python.title: The Zen of Python
python.text: Run import this and Python prints its guiding principles, like "Simple is better than complex".
python.code: import this

python.title: Types without imports
python.text: Since Python 3.9 you can write list[int] and dict[str, int], and since 3.10 — int | None.
python.code:
def find(names: list[str], key: str) -> int | None:
    return names.index(key) if key in names else None

python.title: breakpoint()
python.text: The built-in breakpoint() (3.7+) pauses the program and opens the pdb debugger.

python.title: Banker's rounding
python.text: round() rounds halves to the nearest even number.
python.code: print(round(0.5), round(1.5), round(2.5))  # 0 2 2

python.title: Swap without a temp variable
python.text: Tuples let you swap values in one line.
python.code:
a, b = 1, 2
a, b = b, a
print(a, b)  # 2 1

python.text: Floats are stored in binary and aren't exact. Use math.isclose to compare them and decimal for money.
python.code:
import math
print(0.1 + 0.2 == 0.3)              # False
print(math.isclose(0.1 + 0.2, 0.3))  # True

python.title: Sorting by key
python.text: sorted takes a key, and Python's sort is stable: equal elements keep their original order.
python.code:
ores = [("iron", 3), ("gold", 1), ("coal", 3)]
print(sorted(ores, key=lambda o: o[1]))
# [('gold', 1), ('iron', 3), ('coal', 3)]

python.title: print with sep and end
python.text: print can insert separators and change the line ending for you.
python.code:
print(*["Python", "Java", "Minecraft"], sep=" · ")
print("loading", end="...\n")

python.title: Generators save memory
python.text: A generator expression doesn't build the whole list — it yields items one by one.
python.code:
total = sum(x * x for x in range(10_000_000))
print(total)  # no 10-million-element list

python.title: __slots__
python.text: __slots__ stops an object from having an attribute dict — objects get lighter when you have lots of them.

java.title: var
java.text: Since Java 10 you can skip the type of a local variable — the compiler infers it. The type is still static.
java.code:
var players = new ArrayList<String>();
var count = 10; // int

java.title: Records
java.text: A record (Java 16+) is a data class in one line: constructor, getters, equals, hashCode and toString are generated.

java.title: Text blocks
java.text: Since Java 15 multi-line text goes in triple quotes — no \n and no concatenation.

java.title: switch expressions
java.text: Since Java 14 a switch can return a value, and the -> arrow never falls through to the next case.

java.title: instanceof with a variable
java.text: Since Java 16 instanceof declares a variable of the right type — no manual cast.

java.title: Sealed classes
java.text: sealed (Java 17) limits which classes are allowed to extend a type.

java.title: Patterns in switch
java.text: Since Java 21 switch can match on types and even take records apart.

java.title: Virtual threads
java.text: Java 21 can run millions of lightweight virtual threads — much cheaper than regular ones.

java.title: The Integer cache
java.text: Integer objects from -128 to 127 come from a cache, so == sometimes "works". Compare objects with equals.

java.title: == vs equals for strings
java.text: == compares references, not text. Always use equals for strings.

java.title: Stream API
java.text: Streams let you filter and transform collections with a chain of calls. toList() exists since Java 16.
java.code:
List<String> loud = names.stream()
    .filter(n -> n.length() > 3)
    .map(String::toUpperCase)
    .toList();

java.title: Optional
java.text: Optional says clearly "there may be no value" and helps avoid NullPointerException.
java.code:
Optional<String> name = Optional.ofNullable(player);
System.out.println(name.orElse("Steve"));

java.title: List.of
java.text: List.of, Set.of and Map.of (Java 9+) create immutable collections. Calling add throws an exception.
java.code:
var ores = List.of("coal", "iron", "gold");
ores.add("diamond"); // UnsupportedOperationException

java.title: try-with-resources
java.text: Resources declared in try(...) close automatically — even if an error happens.

java.title: Method references
java.text: Instead of a lambda you can pass a method reference with ::.
java.code:
names.forEach(System.out::println);
names.sort(String::compareToIgnoreCase);

java.title: Remainder of negatives
java.text: % in Java keeps the sign of the dividend. For a "math" remainder use Math.floorMod.
java.code:
System.out.println(-7 % 3);              // -1
System.out.println(Math.floorMod(-7, 3)); // 2

java.title: char is a number
java.text: In arithmetic a char turns into an int.
java.code:
System.out.println('a' + 1);        // 98
System.out.println((char) ('a' + 1)); // b

java.title: Silent overflow
java.text: int overflows without any error and wraps to negative. The Math.*Exact methods throw instead.
java.code:
System.out.println(Integer.MAX_VALUE + 1); // -2147483648
Math.addExact(Integer.MAX_VALUE, 1);       // ArithmeticException

java.title: BigDecimal for exact numbers
java.text: double isn't exact: 0.1 + 0.2 gives 0.30000000000000004. Money is handled with BigDecimal.

java.title: Labeled break
java.text: break with a label exits several nested loops at once.

java.title: instanceof and null
java.text: null instanceof anything is always false, so you don't need a separate null check before instanceof.
java.code:
Object o = null;
System.out.println(o instanceof String); // false

java.title: Handy Map methods
java.text: Map has getOrDefault, merge and computeIfAbsent — fewer null checks.

java.title: Enums with fields
java.text: A Java enum is a full class: its values can have fields, constructors and methods.

java.title: New String methods
java.text: Since Java 11 strings have repeat, isBlank, strip and lines.

java.title: jshell
java.text: Since Java 9 there's jshell — a console to try code without a class or main.
java.code:
$ jshell
jshell> 2 + 2
$1 ==> 4

java.title: Running a single file
java.text: Since Java 11 you can run a .java file without compiling it with javac first.
java.code: $ java Hello.java

java.title: Underscores in numbers
java.text: Just like in Python, long numbers can be split with underscores (Java 7+).
java.code:
long ticks = 24_000L;
int color = 0xFF_7A_1A;

java.title: Effectively final
java.text: A lambda can use a local variable only if it never changes after assignment.

java.title: Mixin in modding
java.text: Fabric uses the Mixin library: it injects your code straight into Minecraft classes while the game loads, without touching the sources.

java.title: The diamond operator
java.text: Since Java 7 you don't have to repeat the generic type on the right — the compiler infers it.
java.code: Map<String, List<Integer>> scores = new HashMap<>();
